answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, then let trust grow only through a slow spiral of small verified deals with different counterparties. A new identity has no bridge to high-value work until it completes many checked low-value jobs. An attacker creating thousands of fake identities must therefore lock a separate stake for each one and pay fees and time for every spiral, while an honest agent pays once. If fraud is found, the stake is slashed, so a fake plume of identities costs far more than it can earn.
